documents.title: Cardiology Annual Follow-up (02/11/2025)
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Amyloid clinic, 02/11/2025

Seen nine months after CABG, complicated course noted (postoperative bleeding, sternal infection, left phrenic nerve injury followed by pulmonology). No angina since surgery. Exertional breathlessness at his pre-surgery baseline; still sleeps propped up, which pulmonology attributes to the diaphragm. Ankles controlled.
Exam: vitals normal. Regular, no murmur. JVP normal. Healed sternotomy. No edema.
Impression: ATTR-wt cardiomyopathy, stable on tafamidis; CAD s/p CABG without angina.
Plan: continue tafamidis 61 mg, furosemide 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg. One year.

Cardiology

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, afternoon slot as he prefers. Wife present.
Interval: CABG last May with a rough recovery, now done with rehab. Left diaphragm paralysis per pulmonology; still sleeps on a wedge. Cardiology letter from February reviewed.
Function: independent in self-care; wife handles driving now beyond town. No falls. TUG 14 s. Mini-Cog 5/5.
PHQ-9 6. Declines counseling again; says getting through the surgery 'took something out of him.'
Meds: carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID, pramipexole ER 1.5 mg, tafamidis 61 mg, furosemide 20 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg, aspirin 81 mg. NKDA.
Exam: hypomimia, R rest tremor, mild rigidity R wrist. Sternotomy healed. Heart regular. Breath sounds reduced L base. Trace ankle edema.
Prevention: Tdap today (last 2014). Flu and COVID done in the fall. Colonoscopy due 2027; will revisit given age and health at that time.
Labs today. Return in 4 months.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ron, your blood count is back to normal after last year's surgeries. Kidney function is at your usual level. Cholesterol is similar to prior years. No medication changes.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Saw pulmonology 6/17. Per Ron: breathing lying down is better, down to two pillows from the wedge; x-ray showed the left diaphragm still sitting high, same as before; no surgery planned, just watching. We haven't received a letter; requested.
No chest pain. Ankles fine. Swallowing fine. Parkinson symptoms about the same, neurology every 6 months.
Exam: vitals as recorded. Heart regular. Decreased breath sounds L base, unchanged. No edema beyond trace.
A/P: L phrenic nerve injury, improving symptomatically, pulmonology observing. ATTR-wt amyloid stable on tafamidis, BMP today. PD stable. CAD s/p CABG, no angina. Return in 4 months.

Four years on tafamidis. Functional status unchanged over the past year. No angina. Edema controlled on furosemide 20 mg daily.

Impression: stable wild-type ATTR cardiomyopathy; CAD s/p CABG.

documents.title: Question about Ron
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is Ron's wife writing on his account. For a few weeks he has been seeing people in the yard who are not there, and he is convinced the neighbors are coming in and taking things from the garage. He is otherwise himself, no fever, eating fine. He has his neurology appointment June 8. Should we wait for that?

documents.title: RE: Question about Ron
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for telling us. Keeping the June 8 neurology visit makes sense; I'll let their office know what you've described so they're prepared. If he becomes confused, feverish, unusually sleepy, or you feel unsafe, call us the same day or go to the ED. Please don't change any of his medications on your own before then.

conditions.label: Parkinson disease with psychosis
conditions.note: Visual hallucinations and paranoid ideation; per neurology

documents.title: Neurology Visit (06/08/2026)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Movement disorders clinic, 06/08/2026

Mr. Hickey, 72, with Parkinson disease, wild-type ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, CABG in 2024 with a complicated course, and achalasia. His wife brings him in for a month of visual hallucinations and rising suspicion of the neighbors, whom he accuses of stealing from him. His regimen has been stable: carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID and pramipexole 1.5 mg daily. Motor symptoms are well controlled; no change in movement.

Exam: vitals normal. Alert, oriented to person, place and time. Rest tremor, bradykinesia and rigidity as before. No signs of infection or delirium.

Impression: Parkinson disease psychosis.

Plan:
1. Taper pramipexole, the most likely contributor: 0.75 mg ER daily for two weeks, then stop. Continue carbidopa/levodopa unchanged.
2. Primary care to check CBC, metabolic panel, TSH, B12 and urinalysis to exclude a medical contributor.
3. Recheck here in three months, sooner if symptoms escalate.

Neurology

documents.title: Office Visit: Hallucinations
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With wife. Neurology note from 6/8 received and reviewed: Parkinson disease psychosis; plan to taper pramipexole and for us to check labs.
Since then: still sees figures at the edge of the yard most evenings; mostly not bothered by them. Accused the neighbor once more about a missing rake (wife found it in the shed). Sleep OK. No fever, cough, urinary symptoms, constipation beyond his usual. No new medicines or supplements; no sleep aids or anything over the counter.
Exam: afebrile, vitals as recorded. Alert, attentive, oriented x3; conversation linear; he describes the figures calmly. Rest tremor R, bradykinesia, rigidity as before. Heart regular. Lungs: reduced L base, unchanged. Abdomen soft. No edema beyond trace.
A/P
1. PD psychosis: following neurology's plan. Pramipexole ER reduced to 0.75 mg daily x 2 weeks then off; new script sent and old dose stopped. Carbidopa/levodopa unchanged. Wife to call if worse, if he wanders or she feels unsafe.
2. Medical contributors: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, UA today.
Phone check at the end of the taper.
